target.title: fix(zai): send current GLM thinking params
target.body:
Closes #97772

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users enable reasoning on Z.ai GLM models but OpenClaw sends a stale or semantically wrong OpenAI-compatible payload, so current GLM reasoning mode is not activated as requested.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenAI-compatible completions formatter now emits the current Z.ai thinking payload shape, `thinking: { type: "enabled" | "disabled" }`, instead of the legacy `enable_thinking` field. The shared Z.ai mapping lives with the OpenAI-compatible completions provider and is used by both request builders, so the normal stream path and the managed provider-transport path stay aligned.

GLM-5.2 receives the provider-supported `reasoning_effort` values (`high` or `max`) when thinking is enabled. `minimal` now preserves OpenClaw's enabled-thinking semantics by normalizing to the low-style enabled path, while `none` and off-style requests still send disabled thinking without `reasoning_effort`. Binary Z.ai thinking models such as GLM-5.1 keep the on/off payload without an unsupported effort field.

## User Impact

Z.ai GLM users can turn reasoning on and have OpenClaw send the request shape expected by the current Z.ai API. Existing binary thinking models keep their current behavior and do not receive extra unsupported `reasoning_effort` parameters.

## Evidence

- Current head: `cca1c8481c67479fca6e2204d3e6051deda3dc73`.
- Claim proved: both OpenAI-compatible completions request builders use `thinking.type`, never `enable_thinking`, for Z.ai thinking mode; GLM-5.2 maps `minimal` and low-style enabled thinking to `reasoning_effort: "high"`, strongest OpenClaw effort to `"max"`, and off/none to disabled thinking; binary GLM-5.1 keeps enabled thinking without `reasoning_effort`.
- Merge refresh: merged latest `upstream/main` (`f6b99012435391f18b701330c7b6f40248e6b61c`) into `codex/97772-zai-thinking` so the PR is on the current base.
- Current-head light verification: `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` -> passed.
- Focused local Vitest/oxfmt proof still needs a dependency-ready environment; this Windows worktree has no `node_modules`, so `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ...` stops with `OPENCLAW_MISSING_VITEST` before tests execute.
- Earlier proof on prior heads remains relevant for the same touched paths: focused payload tests covered the legacy `streamOpenAICompletions` request body and the managed `buildOpenAICompletionsParams` transport path, and live Z.ai proof returned a streaming response with `thinking: { type: "enabled" }`, `reasoning_effort: "high"`, and no `enable_thinking`.
- ClawSweeper follow-up handled on this head: `minimal` no longer maps to disabled thinking; it preserves enabled reasoning semantics in the shared Z.ai helper and both provider/managed transport tests were updated for GLM-5.2 and binary GLM-5.1 behavior.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted: yes. Codex inspected the issue, checked duplicate PR coverage, implemented the focused fix, ran available lightweight validation, addressed ClawSweeper feedback, and refreshed this PR body for the current head.
